solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Christian at Indian festival among two hundred

indicators.note: among says the following pieces sit within the two hundred

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two hundred is CC
Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

explanation.surface: A Christian attends an Indian festival in a crowd of two hundred people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts the following pieces inside CC; Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic is a member of the Roman Catholic Church, one branch of Christianity.

clue.text: Bad tempered passenger's last to be carried by taxi-driver

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cabby is the driver of a cab or taxi

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the passenger

explanation.surface: A grumpy passenger at the end of a taxi ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes R, the end of PASSENGER, and 'to be carried by' puts it inside CABBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby is an informal adjective for irritable or grumpy, the same as bad tempered.

clue.text: Alarm when bed is made the wrong way — something wicked!

indicators.note: a bed made the wrong way round has its letters running backwards

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a sin is a wicked act

explanation.surface: A wrongly made bed is treated as a cause for alarm and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made the wrong way' turns COT into TOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, an old word still used for any alarm.

clue.text: Not in, frequently now wandering away from built-up area?

parts.note: someone not in is out
oft is a poetic word for often

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who is rarely home, often wandering off from the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns NOW into OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of town describes a place in the countryside or suburbs, beyond the town's built-up streets.

clue.text: Disqualifying one captain acting badly

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A single captain's poor acting rules him out of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the captain and acting letters after I, the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacitating means disabling or making unfit, which is what disqualifying does to someone.

clue.text: Essayist and daughter joining a Greek character

parts.note: Charles Lamb was the English essayist who wrote as Elia

explanation.surface: A writer and his daughter join up with a character from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Leave sailor with model

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to sit is to pose as an artist's model

explanation.surface: Permission to go ashore for a sailor and his model.
explanation.walkthrough: Absit is Latin for 'let him be absent', used at older British universities for a student's permission to be away.
explanation.definitionFit: An absit is a formal permission for a student to be absent from college, a kind of leave.

clue.text: Carried money, reportedly, to get wine

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: carried is bore and money is dough, slang for cash

explanation.surface: Someone carries cash to buy a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: BORE DOUGH, said aloud, matches the French wine region's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is red or white wine from the region around the French city of that name.

clue.text: New date set around the end of August to be confirmed

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the August letter
new means made again, so the letters are given a fresh order
the end of asks only for the final letter of August

explanation.surface: A new date, set for late August, awaits confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' shuffles the date and set letters, and 'around' wraps them round T, from 'the end of August'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify, so something attested has been verified.

clue.text: This and that could get our team humming

indicators.note: could get says these letters may be turned into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A football fan hopes something will get the team buzzing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' rearranges OUR TEAM HUMMING.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnium gatherum is a mock-Latin term for a miscellany, a random collection of odds and ends.

clue.text: A doubter not keeping quiet, one for self-denial

indicators.note: not keeping means letting go of a piece, so it is taken out

parts.note: a sceptic is someone who doubts
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A noisy doubter who ends up embracing self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not keeping' removes P from SCEPTIC to leave SCETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-discipline and gives up comforts, a person devoted to abstinence.

clue.text: Ark must get organised for one of a pair therein?

indicators.note: letters that get organised are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Noah's Ark has to be put in order before the animals board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get organised' rearranges ARK MUST; the animals entered Noah's Ark two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: A muskrat is an animal, and the Ark held every animal in pairs, so it is one of a pair aboard.

clue.text: Legal document not long-winded?

definitions.meaning: a barrister's written summary of a case

explanation.surface: A legal paper that is mercifully short.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a lawyer's instructions for a case, and as an adjective it means concise.

clue.text: Instruction not to be so digitally rude is serving no purpose

definitions.text: Instruction not to be so digitally rude
definitions.meaning: pointing with a finger is rude, so an order to do less of it is the answer

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child to stop pointing, which is futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digitally' means with the fingers (digits), not online.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless means futile or without purpose, the second, plain sense of the answer.

clue.text: Major cure — fee terrible — it's something unavoidable

indicators.note: terrible means in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A major medical cure comes with a fearsome fee nobody can avoid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges MAJOR CURE FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Force majeure is the legal term for an irresistible event, such as war or disaster, that excuses a contract.

clue.text: Man stopping short north of a river and beginning to axe tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, north of puts the first piece above the rest
stopping short means the word ends early, losing its final letter

parts.note: Jack is a man's name

indicators.note: beginning to asks for only the first letter of axe

explanation.surface: A man stops beside a river and starts to fell a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopping short' cuts JACK to JAC; 'beginning to axe' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: The jacaranda is a tropical tree known for its clusters of blue-purple flowers.

clue.text: Professional record — one hears that introduction

indicators.note: one hears means the words are taken as said aloud

parts.note: a professional is a pro and a record is a log

explanation.surface: A professional's track record is heard as an introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO LOG, said aloud, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is the opening section of a play or book, which serves as its introduction.

clue.text: Old religious outreach exposing a type of sin?

parts.note: a mission is a religious campaign to spread the faith

explanation.surface: An old church mission reveals some kind of sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Theology distinguishes sins of commission from sins of omission, things left undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Omission names a failure to do something, and a sin of omission is a recognised kind of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Objection about receptacle used in church

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a monstrance is the vessel in which the consecrated Host is displayed

explanation.surface: A protest is lodged over a vessel used in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a formal protest or complaint, an expression of objection.

clue.text: Church is participating in street rock

indicators.note: participating in means taking part within, so the pieces go inside

explanation.surface: A church takes part in a street rock concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like music in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Schist is a metamorphic rock that splits into thin layers.

clue.text: Feature of Cheddar, ultimate bit of food to be eaten with gusto

parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England, beside the village that gave the cheese its name

indicators.note: ultimate bit of asks for only the last letter of food

explanation.surface: Cheddar cheese, the last of the food, is wolfed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheddar' looks like the cheese, but here it is the Somerset village whose famous gorge gives GORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff oneself greedily, so gorged means devoured eagerly.

clue.text: Desperate model longing to hug daughter

indicators.note: to hug is to hold close inside, so the pair wraps the daughter

parts.note: a last is a shoemaker's foot-shaped model
an itch is a restless longing

explanation.surface: A model longs to embrace her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hug' wraps the model-and-longing pair round D; a last is the wooden foot a shoemaker works on.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final, desperate attempt made when all else has failed.

clue.text: No tribe of Israel set up Philistine god

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Gad was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: No tribe of Israel set up an idol to the Philistines' god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns NOGAD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dagon was a deity worshipped by the Philistines in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Page in ministerial residence ushering last couple out

indicators.note: ushering out the last couple shows the final two letters are removed

parts.note: a parish minister's house in the Church of England, named after the clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A page boy at the rectory shows the last couple of guests out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ushering last couple out' drops RY from RECTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf.

clue.text: Making stage entrance and speaking at length

definitions.meaning: an actor ... walks onto the stage

explanation.surface: An actor walks on and then delivers a lengthy speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on means both appearing on stage and rambling tediously, two separate idioms.

clue.text: Position in society possibly organised by top man

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so ran means organised
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A social position possibly arranged by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranking means one's standing or status, a place in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Current line unexpectedly meeting with refusal

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters turn up in an unforeseen order

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A current line of thinking meets with an unexpected refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' turns LINE into ELNI.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is a warm Pacific ocean current that disrupts weather patterns worldwide.

clue.text: Transmitted confession of one not full-time journalist?

parts.note: someone admitting what they are begins 'I'm'
part as in part-time
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A part-time journalist confesses to passing on information.
explanation.walkthrough: The confession reads I'M PART ED, 'I am a part-time editor'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to pass on or communicate information, so imparted means conveyed.
